quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile traveled. Any extra task takes your focus away from driving and creates danger.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under bad weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt normal traffic flow. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: You get the information you need to drive safely mostly by:

options.text: Seeing.
Talking to yourself.
Following other cars.
Turning the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing.
questions.explanation: Almost all the information you need to drive safely comes from seeing. Stay aware of what is around your car. Look ahead to conditions far down the road.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You can go if the way is clear.
Stop completely before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you pass these signs, you are going the wrong way and may have a head-on crash. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible driving speeds for the area.
The fastest or slowest speed you can legally drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you can legally drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the fastest or slowest safe speed allowed on the road. The limits are for perfect conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are worse.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
Your body weight.
How much time passes between drinks.
All three.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol content depends on how much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight. Eating slows alcohol absorption but cannot prevent impairment from too much alcohol.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not need to stop.
Road conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water or puddles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more distance to stop and may skid on turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: You see a railroad crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn down the radio so you can hear an approaching train.
Only go when a flagger tells you it is safe.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less strong when drinking beer instead of wine.
Is less strong when drinking wine instead of beer.
Is strongest when drinking hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol hurts your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
About the same.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see in the dark. Headlights from other cars can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lanes. A cyclist is ahead of you going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the cyclist.
Keep driving. It is the cyclist's job to get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to warn the cyclist you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the cyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on normal roads, or 5 feet on faster roads or with multiple cyclists. Do not honk suddenly as this may scare the cyclist and cause a crash.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: After the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagman, or train horn sounds. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks only.
Trucks are entering the highway.
A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on a yellow background. They warn you about hazards ahead. This sign means a steep hill is coming. Be ready to adjust your speed.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane exists, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear so the tailgater will pass you.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated, move to the right lane if possible. If not, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slow down gradually. This will let the tailgater pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. Who goes first?

options.text: The vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the left.
Drivers should use hand signals to decide.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. The vehicle on the left must yield.

questions.question: The light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before it turns red.
Brake hard and stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Prepare to stop before you reach the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving normally.
Move to the right curb and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, pull over to the right curb or side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: What does a defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly all the time.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at the same speed constantly.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers get distracted. A defensive driver watches other drivers and predicts problems before they happen.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what speed is safest?

options.text: Keep changing your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than the other cars.
Drive slower than the other cars.
Drive at the same speed as the other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as the other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when some drivers go faster or slower than others. Always drive with the flow of traffic, within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is cleaning up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through the work zone.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the bicyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists as much space as you can. Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly can force them off course.

questions.question: When small children ride in a vehicle, they:

options.text: Can be safely held by an adult.
Will be safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Small children need special child seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always keep children properly fastened in a seat.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive the same as you would on dry roads.
Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.
Avoid crossing bridges or intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your vehicle will need more time to stop.

questions.question: When you see an accident scene, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop only if you are involved or if no emergency help has arrived yet.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop unless you are involved in the accident or emergency help has not arrived. Focus on your driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accidents, fires, or other disasters just to look.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street if:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely if you can clearly see the road ahead, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives, and your vehicle is fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently slow down using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently slow down using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep them off the pavement and reduce speed by gently braking. When you are going slow enough, turn the steering wheel to get back on the road. Do not sharply turn the steering wheel to force your vehicle back.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, driving away from a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder when changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.
